children: Oil prices fell in early European trading Friday after surging in the previous session, as traders assessed growing risks to Middle East crude exports following fresh territorial gains by Iran-backed Houthi militants in Yemen.

Front-month Brent crude oil futures fell 2.1% to $105.36 a barrel, while front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures dropped 1.7% to $100.69 a barrel. Both benchmarks settled Thursday at their highest closing levels since May 19, with Brent at $107.63 and WTI at $102.48.

Shipping around the Strait of Hormuz remained under pressure, with the U.K. Maritime Trade Operations saying Thursday that four unidentified projectiles struck two vessels near Khasab, Oman, causing a fire on one.

Meanwhile, Houthi militants seized the strategic Yemeni port city of Mokha, strengthening their position near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. The advance raises fresh risks around the Red Sea at a time when Saudi Arabia has increasingly relied on the route to circumvent disruptions in the Persian Gulf. The kingdom's crude production fell by roughly 1.9 million barrels a day to 6.24 million barrels a day in August, down 23% from July, according to the latest data from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries.
ANZ Research analysts said the advance could give the Houthis a foothold that would enable the group to almost fully control the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.

The pullback in crude follows a sharp rally Thursday, when WTI surged 6.7% and Brent gained 6.3% as intensifying fighting across the region fueled concerns over global energy supplies. Oil futures had moved into overbought territory and could be due for a corrective phase, Dennis Kissler of BOK Financial said in a note.

title: Oil Prices Slip After Recent Surge Amid Supply Risks
